lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.13 - A Listen, point, and say

details: Listen, point, and say checks understanding of new vocabulary.. Listen and point shows students can match what they hear to the right image. Say practises first-step pronunciation.
Look for careful listening, correct pointing, confident repetition and clear pronunciation.
“Class, I’m not sure I want to be a teacher anymore. I want to do something different. I love drawing (mime) and acting (mime) and sports too! What jobs do you like? Let's take a look!'”

Heads Up: 
Focus the students’ attention on the CPT and present relevant features of the language (MFP). Then demonstrate the activity with TA/students.
Heads Down: 
Ss open their books. Instruct and ask ICQs. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
Heads Together: 
Demo/Instruct and ask ICQs, including setting behaviour expectations. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
Reward moment
Check behaviour expectations and reward with APOS or remind for 4Rs

lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.13 - B. Listen and circle

details: Listen and circle continues checking sound–image connection. Students practise listening for specific information and clearly circling an image.
Look for careful listening, accurate choices and pencil grip.
“These jobs look fun - really fun! Do you want to learn more? I do! Let's find out, what do they do?”

lessonPlan.topic: Activity Book p.67 - A Decode, write, and match

details: Decode, write and match has students spell out different jobs to practise spellings and penmanship. They then match each job to a picture.
Look for careful penmanship, correct spelling and accurate matches.
“There’s so many jobs I could try. How many jobs are there? Let's count... Wow so many! I can't remember them all. Can you help me? What are they?”

lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.14 - C. Ask and answer

details: Ask and answer gives students controlled practice using the target language to ask and respond to simple questions using the first and second person..
Look for accurate use and pronunciation of “What do you want to be?” and “I want to be ___” and natural turn-taking with classmates.
“You’ve been really helpful. I really want to go to the moon. So I want to be an astronaut. How about you?”

lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.14 - D. Ask and answer

details: Ask and answer gives students controlled practice using the target language to ask and respond to simple questions using the third person.
Look for accurate use of the pronouns ‘he’ and ‘she’ and the third person present tense form of ‘want’ as ‘wants’.
“What about your classmates? Can you find out what jobs they want to have? Let’s ask - what do you want to be?”
